results.name: db

findings.message: runs with 1 replica: an interruption means downtime
findings.remediation:
Run at least 2 replicas (3 across zones is better), or give the HPA minReplicas: 2.

# StatefulSet: spec
replicas: 2

findings.message: container "db" has no readinessProbe: traffic can reach a pod that is not ready
findings.remediation:
Add a readinessProbe so traffic only reaches pods that can serve it. Point it at your health endpoint.

# spec.template.spec.containers[db]
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8080
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 3

findings.message: uses persistent volumes: zonal disks make rescheduling slower and tied to one zone
findings.remediation:
A zonal volume keeps the pod in one zone and slows rescheduling. Keep this workload on on-demand nodes, or accept slower recovery.

# spec.template.spec
nodeSelector:
  karpenter.sh/capacity-type: on-demand

findings.message: no preStop hook: in-flight requests may be cut when the node is reclaimed
findings.remediation:
Add a short preStop sleep so the endpoint is removed from load balancers before the process gets SIGTERM.

# spec.template.spec.containers[db]
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["sleep", "15"]

confidenceReasons: persistent state: the manifest does not show how the application replicates or recovers it
StatefulSet: pod identity and ordering matter, and the manifest does not show how much

findings.message: terminationGracePeriodSeconds is 300s, but Spot gives only 120s of notice
findings.remediation:
Make the application exit on SIGTERM within the 2-minute Spot notice and lower the grace period.

# spec.template.spec
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 90

findings.message: no topology spread or pod anti-affinity: replicas can land on the same node or zone
findings.remediation:
Spread the replicas across zones and nodes.

# spec.template.spec
topologySpreadConstraints:
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
    whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
    labelSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app: worker
  - maxSkew: 1
    topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
    whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
    labelSelector:
      matchLabels:
        app: worker

findings.message: no PodDisruptionBudget: draining can remove too many replicas at once
findings.remediation:
Add a PodDisruptionBudget so a drain removes one replica at a time.

apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: worker
  namespace: shop
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 1
  unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: worker

findings.message: container "worker" has no readinessProbe: traffic can reach a pod that is not ready
findings.remediation:
Add a readinessProbe so traffic only reaches pods that can serve it. Point it at your health endpoint.

# spec.template.spec.containers[worker]
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8080
  periodSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 3

findings.message: no preStop hook: in-flight requests may be cut when the node is reclaimed
findings.remediation:
Add a short preStop sleep so the endpoint is removed from load balancers before the process gets SIGTERM.

# spec.template.spec.containers[worker]
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["sleep", "15"]

findings.message: supports only one Availability Zone: that zone running out of Spot capacity leaves the pool without nodes
findings.remediation:
Let the NodePool use every zone that has a subnet, or list at least two.

# NodePool spec.template.spec.requirements
- key: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
  operator: In
  values: ["<zone-a>", "<zone-b>", "<zone-c>"]

findings.message: allows only 2 instance families (at least 3 recommended)
findings.remediation:
Allow several instance categories and make Karpenter keep a minimum of families.

# NodePool spec.template.spec.requirements
- key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-category
  operator: In
  values: ["c", "m", "r"]
- key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-family
  operator: Exists
  minValues: 5

findings.message: allows only 4 instance types (AWS recommends at least 10 for Spot)
findings.remediation:
List more instance types, or better, constrain by category and generation and let Karpenter pick the types.

# NodePool spec.template.spec.requirements
- key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-category
  operator: In
  values: ["c", "m", "r"]
- key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-generation
  operator: Gt
  values: ["2"]
- key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
  operator: Exists
  minValues: 10

findings.message: no explicit disruption budget: Karpenter applies its default of 10% of nodes at a time
findings.remediation:
Set a disruption budget that fits you. Remove a budget of 0 nodes that is always active, or limit it with a schedule.

# NodePool spec.disruption
budgets:
  - nodes: "10%"
  - nodes: "0"          # block voluntary disruption only during business hours
    schedule: "0 9 * * mon-fri"
    duration: 8h

findings.message: no minValues on instance type, family or category: nothing makes Karpenter keep a minimum of instance diversity
findings.remediation:
Make Karpenter keep a minimum of instance diversity.

# NodePool spec.template.spec.requirements
- key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-family
  operator: Exists
  minValues: 5
